0.long_answer: A cerebral arteriovenous malformation (AVM) is the most common type of brain vascular malformation. This lesion is characterized by abnormal, direct connections between arteries and veins, bypassing the normal capillary network that would typically slow blood flow and disperse pressure. The absence of capillaries leads to high pressure in the veins, increasing the risk of vessel rupture and potentially causing an intracranial hemorrhage. Cerebral AVMs are usually congenital but may remain asymptomatic until later in life when complications such as bleeding, seizures, or neurological deficits arise. Diagnosis is typically confirmed through imaging studies like CT, MRI, or angiography, and treatment options include surgical resection, endovascular embolization, or radiosurgery depending on the size and location of the AVM.
